page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highmem-8 is an x86_64 architecture server instance configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 64 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core, positioning the instance within the memory-optimized resource class. The instance features dedicated CPU allocation, ensuring consistent compute performance without the resource sharing or credit-depletion risks associated with burstable instances.

This server type does not include local NVMe SSD storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached block storage. Additionally, the instance does not feature integrated GPU hardware accelerators and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. These design choices prioritize memory density and dedicated compute over local storage speed or graphical processing capabilities.

The n4d-highmem-8 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, which provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require substantial memory footprints but do not demand high core counts. This resource balance is appropriate for memory-intensive workloads such as medium-sized databases, in-memory caching layers, enterprise applications, and data buffering tasks.
